etymology: From Greek Iēsous, transliterating Hebrew Yeshua (יֵשׁוּעַ) — short for Yehoshua, "YHWH saves."
biblical_def: The proper name of the eternal Son of God incarnate, given by the angel "for he shall save his people from their sins" (Matt 1:21).
webster_summary: The Savior of men, the Christ.
webster_full: The Savior of men, the Christ, the Anointed of God, sent into the world to save sinners by His death and resurrection. The name above every name.
scriptures: Matthew 1:21
And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.
Acts 4:12
Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
Philippians 2:9-10
Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.
corruption_summary: The name reduced to casual exclamation or vague spiritual figure stripped of His specific saving work.
corruption_paragraphs: Modern usage drains the name of content. Used as profanity or as a sentimental "Jesus loves everybody" cliché, the actual scriptural Jesus — incarnate, crucified, risen, returning Judge — disappears. Recovering the name means recovering the man and the mission: the Word made flesh who saves sinners by substitutionary death.
usage: Jesus is the only name given for salvation.
Pray in His name; serve in His name; bow before His name.

etymology: From Greek Christos (Χριστός) — "anointed," translating Hebrew Mashiach (Messiah).
biblical_def: The Anointed One — Prophet, Priest, and King — promised in the Old Testament and revealed as Jesus of Nazareth (John 1:41; 20:31).
webster_summary: The Anointed; the title given to Jesus.
webster_full: The Anointed One; the title and office of Jesus, in whom the threefold anointing of Prophet, Priest, and King is fulfilled. Synonymous with Messiah.
scriptures: John 1:41
He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.
Matthew 16:16
Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
1 John 5:1
Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God.
corruption_summary: Treated as Jesus' surname rather than His office and identity as the Anointed Deliverer.
corruption_paragraphs: When 'Christ' becomes a last name, the loaded weight of the title evaporates. He is not Jesus Christ the way someone is John Smith — He is Jesus the Christ, the long-awaited Anointed One who fulfills the entire Old Testament shadow-system.
usage: Confess Jesus as the Christ — the office matters.
He is anointed Prophet, Priest, and King.

etymology: Fourth Servant Song in Isaiah, ~700 BC.
biblical_def: The Suffering Servant prophecy — the clearest Old Testament portrait of the substitutionary atonement of the Messiah.
webster_summary: Isaiah's prophecy of the suffering Messiah.
webster_full: The chapter in which Isaiah foresees the Servant of YHWH bearing the iniquities of His people, pierced for transgressions, silent before His accusers, justifying many by His knowledge.
scriptures: Isaiah 53:5
He was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
Isaiah 53:6
All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.
The place of the scripture which he read was this... and Philip... preached unto him Jesus.
corruption_summary: Reread as Israel-as-corporate-suffering rather than the personal Messiah.
corruption_paragraphs: Modern Jewish exegesis often spreads Isaiah 53 across the nation as the suffering people; New Testament writers and the early church saw a single, personal, substitutionary Sufferer — Jesus the Christ. Acts 8 settles it: Philip read 'this scripture' and 'preached unto him Jesus.'
roots_summary: Hebrew ebed YHWH — Servant of the LORD.
usage: Read Isaiah 53 every Good Friday.
It is the gospel preached 700 years early.

etymology: Paul's resurrection chapter, ~AD 55.
biblical_def: Paul's full doctrinal exposition of the bodily resurrection — Christ's, ours, and the eschatological transformation of the body.
webster_summary: The resurrection chapter.
webster_full: Paul's defense of the bodily resurrection of Christ as the gospel itself, with witnesses listed; the doctrinal explanation of our future resurrection body; and the trumpet-call victory over death.
scriptures: 1 Corinthians 15:3-4
I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day.
1 Corinthians 15:14
If Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.
1 Corinthians 15:55-57
O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? ... thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
corruption_summary: Reduced to a chapter on heaven; the bodily, physical, eschatological transformation evaporates.
corruption_paragraphs: Funeral sermons quote 15:55 about death's sting but skip the body. Paul insists: spiritual body, imperishable body, transformed body — not disembodied soul-floating. The hope is resurrection, not departure.
usage: Read 1 Corinthians 15 to recover bodily resurrection hope.
Christ's resurrection is the firstfruits of ours.

etymology: Opening chapter of the Hebrew Torah, ~1400 BC traditional dating.
biblical_def: The creation account — God creating the heavens and earth in six days by His word, declaring it good, and resting the seventh.
webster_summary: The creation chapter.
webster_full: The opening chapter of Scripture in which God speaks the cosmos into existence in six days, climaxing with humanity in His image, male and female, with dominion.
scriptures: Genesis 1:1
In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
Genesis 1:27
So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
Genesis 1:31
And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.
corruption_summary: Reframed as ancient mythology or evolutionary process to harmonize with naturalism.
corruption_paragraphs: Genesis 1 is treated as poetic primitive science by some, or as a problem to solve by others. The text presents itself as the foundational account: God created — by word, by week, with humanity in His image. Whatever else we say, that has to stand.
usage: Read Genesis 1 to anchor your worldview.
Image-of-God dignity comes from this chapter.

etymology: Shorthand for the twelve apostles called by Jesus (Matt 10:1-4); also the Hebrew Bible's twelve Minor Prophets.
biblical_def: Either (1) the twelve apostles chosen by Christ as foundational witnesses of the gospel, or (2) the Book of the Twelve — the twelve Minor Prophets gathered as one scroll.
webster_summary: The twelve apostles or twelve minor prophets.
webster_full: A double-meaning phrase in Scripture: the twelve apostles whom Jesus appointed; or the Book of the Twelve, the gathered Minor Prophets from Hosea through Malachi.
scriptures: Matthew 10:1
And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits.
Mark 3:14
And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach.
Revelation 21:14
And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
corruption_summary: Dismissed as a marketing roster instead of a deliberate fulfillment of the twelve tribes.
corruption_paragraphs: Twelve is not arbitrary. Twelve tribes, twelve apostles, twelve foundations of the New Jerusalem. Christ rebuilds Israel around Himself by appointing twelve. The number tells the story.
usage: The Twelve carry the witness of Christ to the world.
The Twelve Prophets are read together for one message.

etymology: Old English biter "sharp, painful," from Proto-Germanic root meaning to bite.
biblical_def: A settled resentment of soul that refuses forgiveness and poisons community; the opposite of grace-rooted love (Heb 12:15).
webster_summary: A poisoned, resentful, unforgiving spirit.
webster_full: Sharpness or harshness of taste; figuratively, severe pain or grief; settled hostility; a refusal to release offense that defiles the bearer and those near.
scriptures: Hebrews 12:15
Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled.
Ephesians 4:31
Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.
Acts 8:23
I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.
corruption_summary: Justified as honest pain or self-protection rather than named as defiling sin.
corruption_paragraphs: Therapy culture validates bitterness as righteous response to harm, but Scripture calls it a defiling root that poisons many. Pain is real; bitterness is the choice to nurse it. Forgiveness is not approval — it is release into God's justice.
usage: Pull bitter roots up before they defile many.
Pray for those who hurt you; refuse the inner curse.

etymology: Old English weorc "deed, labor," from Proto-Germanic werkam.
biblical_def: Purposeful labor — created good before the fall (Gen 2:15), cursed at the fall (Gen 3:17-19), redeemed in Christ as service rendered to the Lord (Col 3:23).
webster_summary: Purposeful labor; deed; vocation.
webster_full: Bodily or mental labor; that which is performed; deed; achievement; a person's occupation. Scripturally a creation good, fallen into toil, redeemed unto worship.
scriptures: Genesis 2:15
And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.
Colossians 3:23
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.
2 Thessalonians 3:10
If any would not work, neither should he eat.
corruption_summary: Detached from worship and reduced to either drudgery or self-actualization.
corruption_paragraphs: Work is not the curse — toil is. Work was Eden before the fall and will be the New Jerusalem after the renewal. The corruption is to treat work as merely transactional or as a vehicle for self-realization rather than as worship rendered to the Lord.
roots_summary: Hebrew avodah — work and worship together.
usage: Work as worship; serve as unto the Lord.
Lazy hands and exploitative work both fail the standard.

etymology: Matthew's parable-discourse chapter, ~AD 60.
biblical_def: Matthew's collected kingdom parables — sower, wheat and tares, mustard seed, leaven, hidden treasure, pearl, dragnet — revealing the kingdom in mystery form.
webster_summary: The kingdom-parables chapter.
webster_full: The chapter of Matthew gathering Christ's parables of the kingdom of heaven: how it is sown, mixed with weeds, grows from smallness, hides treasure, gathers all kinds, and separates at the end.
scriptures: Matthew 13:11
Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
Matthew 13:31-32
The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed... the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.
Matthew 13:44
The kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.
corruption_summary: Read for moral tips instead of as kingdom revelation that conceals from the proud.
corruption_paragraphs: The parables are not folk-wisdom illustrations — they are revelatory and selective. Jesus says they hide the kingdom from the unrepentant while opening it to disciples. Treat them as keys that turn only in soft hearts.
usage: Read Matthew 13 to receive the mysteries of the kingdom.
The kingdom comes hidden, then unveiled.

etymology: John's millennial-and-judgment chapter, ~AD 95.
biblical_def: The chapter unfolding Satan's binding, the thousand-year reign, the final rebellion, and the great white throne judgment.
webster_summary: The millennium and final judgment chapter.
webster_full: The Apocalypse's chapter on the binding of Satan, the thousand-year reign of Christ with His martyrs, the loosing for a final battle, and the great white throne where the dead are judged from the books.
scriptures: Revelation 20:4
And I saw thrones... and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
Revelation 20:11
And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away.
Revelation 20:15
And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.
corruption_summary: Reduced to chart-wars over millennial timing instead of received as a call to faithfulness under judgment.
corruption_paragraphs: Premillennial, postmillennial, amillennial — the timing matters less than the warning. Whatever your chart, the great white throne stands. Books are opened. The lamb's-book-of-life is the only refuge. Live now in light of that day.
usage: Read Revelation 20 to be sobered by judgment.
The book of life is the only refuge.

etymology: Mark's chapter of three power-displays, ~AD 60.
biblical_def: Mark's chapter showcasing Christ's authority over demons (Gerasene), disease (woman with hemorrhage), and death (Jairus' daughter).
webster_summary: Mark's chapter of demon, disease, and death undone.
webster_full: The chapter of Mark in which Jesus delivers the Gerasene demoniac, heals the bleeding woman who touched His garment, and raises Jairus' daughter — three displays of authority over the great enemies.
scriptures: Mark 5:9
And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.
Mark 5:34
Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
Mark 5:41
Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.
corruption_summary: Treated as three unrelated miracle stories rather than a deliberate display of Christ's total authority.
corruption_paragraphs: Mark's three stories form one argument: Jesus has authority over demons, disease, and death — the three terrors under which fallen humanity lives. The chapter is not a stack of miracles; it is a coronation of the King over the powers.
usage: Read Mark 5 to see Christ's authority over what terrifies you.
Demons, disease, and death all bow.

etymology: Hebrew Zekaryah (זְכַרְיָה) — "YHWH remembers."
biblical_def: Post-exilic prophet (~520 BC) whose visions encouraged temple rebuilding and foretold the coming Branch — Messiah pierced, returning, and reigning.
webster_summary: Post-exilic prophet of the coming Messiah.
webster_full: A prophet of the post-exilic period whose night visions, oracles of the Branch, and foretelling of the King riding humble on a donkey, the pierced one, and the returning Lord on the Mount of Olives, are densely Messianic.
scriptures: Zechariah 9:9
Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion... behold, thy King cometh unto thee... lowly, and riding upon an ass.
Zechariah 12:10
They shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him.
Zechariah 14:4
And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives.
corruption_summary: Ignored as a minor prophet when in fact he is among the most quoted in the Passion narratives.
corruption_paragraphs: The Passion narratives lean on Zechariah constantly: triumphal entry on a donkey, thirty pieces of silver, the shepherd struck and the sheep scattered, the pierced one. Read Zechariah and the gospels read differently.
usage: Read Zechariah before reading the Passion.
The Branch is the Messiah.

etymology: Phrase used of the seven 'signs' (Greek sēmeia) John records in his gospel.
biblical_def: The seven miraculous signs in John's gospel — water to wine, official's son, lame man, feeding 5000, walking on water, blind man, Lazarus — each unveiling Christ's identity.
webster_summary: John's seven structured signs of Jesus.
webster_full: The seven 'signs' (sēmeia) deliberately structured in the Gospel of John: turning water to wine, healing the official's son, healing the lame man at Bethesda, feeding the 5000, walking on water, healing the man born blind, and raising Lazarus.
scriptures: John 2:11
This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory.
And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book: but these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ.
Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth.
corruption_summary: Treated as random miracles instead of as deliberately structured revelation.
corruption_paragraphs: John tells us the structure: 'these are written that ye might believe.' The seven signs are not a highlight reel; they are an evangelistic argument. Read them as such.
usage: Trace the seven signs in John for evangelism.
Each sign answers a question about Jesus' identity.

etymology: Hebrew Yehudah (יְהוּדָה) — "praise."
biblical_def: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah; the tribe and southern kingdom that bore the messianic line; the tribe of David and Jesus.
webster_summary: Fourth son of Jacob; tribe of David and Jesus.
webster_full: The fourth son of Jacob, head of the tribe that produced David and Jesus; the southern kingdom after the divided monarchy. The lion of Judah is one of Christ's titles.
scriptures: Genesis 49:10
The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come.
Hebrews 7:14
It is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda.
Revelation 5:5
Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed.
corruption_summary: Reduced to a tribal label, missing the royal-priestly thread that runs through the whole canon.
corruption_paragraphs: Judah is not just a tribe — it is the channel of the scepter, the lineage of David, the womb of the Messiah. From Genesis 49 to Revelation 5, the lion of Judah is the through-line of the King.
usage: The Lion of Judah is Christ.
From Judah came the King; from Levi the priests; in Jesus, both.

etymology: Hebrews 4:16 — Greek thronos tēs charitos.
biblical_def: The mercy seat of God now reframed for the new covenant — where believers approach boldly through Christ to receive mercy and grace in time of need (Heb 4:16).
webster_summary: God's seat of mercy approached through Christ.
webster_full: The throne of God considered as the seat of grace and mercy for those who come through Jesus the great High Priest; replaces the inaccessible mercy seat of the old covenant.
scriptures: Hebrews 4:16
Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
Hebrews 10:19
Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus.
Romans 8:34
Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.
corruption_summary: Approached casually, as if the boldness erased the holiness rather than rested on the blood.
corruption_paragraphs: Boldness is real but it is not flippancy. We come boldly because of the blood, not because we have outgrown reverence. The throne is still a throne; the grace is what makes the approach possible.
roots_summary: Greek thronos charitos — throne of grace.
usage: Come boldly to the throne of grace.
The mercy seat is now open through Christ.

etymology: Composite term for figures fulfilling the 'spirit and power of Elijah' (Luke 1:17).
biblical_def: A prophetic forerunner who calls Israel back from idolatry — Elijah himself, John the Baptist, and the eschatological 'Elijah' to come (Mal 4:5; Matt 17:11-13).
webster_summary: Forerunner who calls Israel back to YHWH.
webster_full: A prophetic figure who confronts royal idolatry, calls covenant Israel to repentance, and prepares the way for divine visitation. Originally Elijah; reapplied to John the Baptist; promised again before the Day of the Lord.
scriptures: Malachi 4:5
Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD.
Luke 1:17
And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children.
Matthew 17:12
Elias is come already, and they knew him not.
corruption_summary: Read mechanically as reincarnation rather than typologically as office and ministry.
corruption_paragraphs: John was not Elijah reincarnated — he was Elijah-shaped: same spirit, same wilderness, same confrontation of compromised kings. The Bible deals in types, not transmigration.
roots_summary: Hebrew Eliyahu — my God is YHWH.
usage: John came in the spirit and power of Elijah.
Pray for Elijah-figures in compromised seasons.

etymology: From Old French biauté, from Latin bellus "pretty."
biblical_def: The created harmony, fittingness, and glory that reflects the character of God; one of the transcendentals along with truth and goodness (Ps 27:4).
webster_summary: Created harmony reflecting God's character.
webster_full: That assemblage of properties which excites pleasure in the sight or contemplation; in Scripture, an attribute of God Himself and a feature of His creation, His worship, and His holiness.
scriptures: Psalm 27:4
One thing have I desired of the LORD... to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to enquire in his temple.
Psalm 96:9
O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.
Isaiah 33:17
Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty.
corruption_summary: Reduced to subjective preference or marketed appearance, severed from holiness and truth.
corruption_paragraphs: When beauty is severed from goodness and truth, it becomes either tyranny of appearance or relativist preference. Scripture binds them together: the King is beautiful because He is holy. Worship recovers the binding.
usage: Worship in the beauty of holiness.
Recover beauty as a transcendental.

etymology: From Aaron, brother of Moses, and Greek hierateuma — priesthood.
biblical_def: The Levitical priestly line descended from Aaron, set apart in Exodus 28-29 to mediate the old covenant sacrifices; fulfilled and surpassed by Christ in the order of Melchizedek (Heb 7).
webster_summary: The old covenant priestly line through Aaron.
webster_full: The hereditary priesthood of Israel descending from Aaron, brother of Moses, charged with offering sacrifices, tending the tabernacle, and pronouncing blessing. A shadow of the true priesthood of Christ.
scriptures: Exodus 28:1
Take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother... that he may minister unto me in the priest's office.
Hebrews 7:11
If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood... what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec?
Hebrews 7:23-24
They truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death: but this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.
corruption_summary: Read as still-active in some traditions, missing Hebrews' argument that Christ has fulfilled and ended its mediatorial role.
corruption_paragraphs: Hebrews settles the matter: the Aaronic priesthood was a shadow of the better priesthood. Christ is the great High Priest in Melchizedek's order — once for all, never to die. To rebuild Levitical mediation is to step backwards into shadow.
usage: The Aaronic priesthood pointed to Christ.
Christ's Melchizedek priesthood is the better one.

etymology: From Latin rebellare "to wage war against," re- + bellum war.
biblical_def: Active resistance to legitimate authority, especially God's; equated with the sin of witchcraft (1 Sam 15:23) and the root of the fall.
webster_summary: Open resistance to God's authority.
webster_full: Open and active resistance to lawful authority, especially divine; in Scripture, the essence of sin from Eden through the wilderness through Korah's challenge to Moses.
scriptures: 1 Samuel 15:23
For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.
Numbers 16:1-3
Now Korah... rose up before Moses... and they gathered themselves together against Moses.
Hebrews 3:8
Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness.
corruption_summary: Reframed as authenticity, courage, or resistance to oppression rather than sin.
corruption_paragraphs: The age glamorizes rebellion — speak truth to power, break the rules, follow your heart. Scripture diagnoses unauthorized rebellion as the witchcraft of self-rule. Authority can be misused; rebellion against God is never righteous.
usage: Name rebellion as sin, not authenticity.
Submit to legitimate authority for the Lord's sake.

etymology: Old English cildru, plural of cild "child."
biblical_def: A heritage from the Lord (Ps 127:3) — image-bearers entrusted to parents for nurture in the discipline and instruction of the Lord (Eph 6:4).
webster_summary: A heritage from the Lord.
webster_full: The young of human kind; offspring; in Scripture, a blessing, a heritage, a stewardship to be raised in the fear and admonition of the Lord.
scriptures: Psalm 127:3
Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.
Ephesians 6:4
Ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Matthew 19:14
Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
corruption_summary: Treated as accessories to lifestyle, burden to opt out of, or future consumers — not as image-bearers and heritage.
corruption_paragraphs: Modern Western culture has reframed children as choice, cost, and inconvenience. Scripture calls them heritage, blessing, and the kingdom's natural belonging. Recover the joy of children as gift; recover parenting as discipleship.
roots_summary: Hebrew yeled — child; Greek teknon — child.
usage: Children are heritage, not optional accessory.
Bring them up in the nurture of the Lord.

etymology: Hebrew Yisra'el (יִשְׂרָאֵל) — "strives with God" or "God strives."
biblical_def: The covenant people descended from Jacob (renamed Israel), set apart through Abraham, redeemed through the exodus, and gathered in the Messiah; the church grafted in (Rom 11).
webster_summary: The covenant people of God.
webster_full: The descendants of Jacob through whom God committed His oracles; the elect nation of the old covenant; in the new covenant the believing remnant joined by Gentiles grafted into the olive tree.
scriptures: Genesis 32:28
Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.
Romans 9:6
Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel.
Romans 11:26
And so all Israel shall be saved.
corruption_summary: Conflated only with the modern political state, missing the deep theological category Paul develops.
corruption_paragraphs: Romans 9-11 forces nuance: Israel after the flesh, the Israel of God, all Israel. The modern nation-state is one strand; the covenant people of God across the ages is another. Read Paul slowly.
usage: The Israel of God is the people of faith.
Pray for the peace of Israel after the flesh too.

etymology: Jesus' upper-room vine discourse, ~AD 33.
biblical_def: The chapter of the True Vine — abiding in Christ, bearing fruit, and the love-and-hatred experienced by His friends.
webster_summary: The True Vine and abiding chapter.
webster_full: The Upper Room discourse chapter where Jesus declares Himself the True Vine, His disciples the branches, and apart from Him they can do nothing — followed by His command to love and warning of the world's hatred.
scriptures: John 15:5
I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
John 15:13
Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
John 15:18
If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.
corruption_summary: Reduced to inspirational fruit-bearing without the life-and-death stakes of abiding and the world's hatred.
corruption_paragraphs: John 15 is not a productivity chapter — it is a chapter about life or death union. Branches that don't abide are gathered and burned. The same chapter that promises fruit warns of hatred. Take both sides seriously.
usage: Abide in Christ; bear much fruit.
Expect the world's hatred; love each other deeply.

etymology: From Latin pastor "shepherd," applied to Christian leaders.
biblical_def: The qualifications and dispositions of one who shepherds Christ's flock — above reproach, gentle, sober, hospitable, apt to teach, not greedy (1 Tim 3:1-7; Titus 1:5-9; 1 Pet 5:1-4).
webster_summary: The character required of Christ's shepherds.
webster_full: The integrated cluster of qualifications Scripture requires of those who oversee Christ's church — above reproach in life, sober, gentle, hospitable, faithful in marriage and household, apt to teach, not greedy, not new in the faith.
scriptures: 1 Timothy 3:2
A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach.
Titus 1:7-8
For a bishop must be blameless... not soon angry... but a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate.
1 Peter 5:2-3
Feed the flock of God which is among you... not for filthy lucre... neither as being lords over God's heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.
corruption_summary: Replaced by competence-focused leadership culture — vision, charisma, platform — instead of integrated character.
corruption_paragraphs: Scripture's pastoral qualifications are mostly character. Modern church culture grades on charisma, platform, and growth metrics. The two regularly produce different shortlists. The crash of celebrity pastors is the warning bell.
usage: Vet pastoral candidates by character before competence.
Watch your life and doctrine closely.

etymology: From Latin vulnerabilis "capable of being wounded," from vulnus "wound."
biblical_def: Honest exposure of weakness, sin, and need before God and trusted others — not a virtue in itself, but the soil where confession, healing, and union grow (James 5:16; 2 Cor 12:9).
webster_summary: Honest exposure of weakness before God and others.
webster_full: The state of being open to wound; in pastoral and discipling language, the willingness to expose weakness, sin, and dependence rather than perform strength. Required for confession, accountability, and genuine community.
scriptures: James 5:16
Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.
2 Corinthians 12:9
My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
Psalm 51:17
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
corruption_summary: Promoted as a virtue in itself or weaponized as oversharing-for-attention; severed from confession and pursuit of holiness.
corruption_paragraphs: Pop psychology made vulnerability a virtue. Scripture treats exposure as the means, not the end — confess so you may be healed; weakness so His strength may rest. Vulnerability without confession is performance; confession without holiness is therapy.
usage: Be vulnerable with confession, not just with feelings.
Strength rests on the broken-and-contrite heart.
